title: open-source natural-history pass (GBD disability weights + PMC survival) — D lift / M corroboration

gbd_disability_join.evidence_basis: GeneReviews NBK1261 (Pompe Disease) Clinical Description: progressive muscle weakness and motor impairment; intellect typically normal
GeneReviews NBK1162 (MPS I) Clinical Description: progressive cognitive decline with motor and skeletal disease in the severe (Hurler) phenotype
GeneReviews NBK1370 (Acid Sphingomyelinase Deficiency, type A): rapidly progressive neurodegeneration, loss of motor and cognitive milestones
MedGen clinical_definition: HbH disease chronic hemolytic anemia of moderate severity
GeneReviews NBK1119 (Dystrophinopathies) Clinical Description: loss of independent ambulation, wheelchair use by early teens
MedGen clinical_definition: severe anemia from infancy requiring regular transfusion (transfusion-dependent beta-thalassemia / Cooley anemia)
GeneReviews NBK1495 (Hemophilia B): recurrent joint bleeding leads to progressive, disabling arthropathy without prophylaxis
GeneReviews NBK1404 (Hemophilia A): recurrent joint bleeding leads to progressive, disabling arthropathy without prophylaxis
MedGen clinical_definition: without treatment, neurological damage and intellectual disability
GeneReviews NBK1504 (Phenylalanine Hydroxylase Deficiency): untreated classic PKU causes profound, irreversible intellectual disability

gbd_excluded.reason: multi-domain: chronic hemolytic anemia + episodic vaso-occlusive pain crises + cumulative ischemic organ damage (stroke, acute chest, splenic/renal). No single GBD health state captures the dominant sequela without gross under-statement; D left [O] (not guessed)
multi-system: progressive obstructive lung disease + exocrine pancreatic insufficiency + nutritional/GI involvement; no single dominant GBD state. D left [O]

variable and pyridoxine(B6)-responsive in a major subset; multi-domain (intellectual disability + ectopia lentis + skeletal marfanoid + thromboembolism); no single dominant untreated state. D left at banked grade (not lifted)
multi-domain (progressive renal + cardiac + cerebrovascular + neuropathic pain + GI); no single dominant disability state. D left [O]
variable hepatic vs neuropsychiatric presentation; highly treatable; no single dominant untreated disability state. D left [O]
dominant life-threat is aortic dissection/rupture (captured on the mortality axis); chronic functional disability is variable (skeletal/ocular). No single dominant disability state. D left [O]
disability is stage-dependent (slowly progressive CKD reaching ESRD typically in later adulthood, and not in all); no single fixed-tier dominant state for the untreated natural history. D left [O]
perinatal-lethal skeletal dysplasia: death in utero or neonatally precludes a chronic disability phase (whole burden is on onset/mortality). D left [O]

untreated natural history is mortality-dominant (acute liver failure, hepatocellular carcinoma, neurological crises); no single chronic disability state distinct from the lethal course (burden on the mortality axis). D left [O]

pmc_mortality_corroborations.sentence: The condition is often lethal, with death usually occurring either in utero or in the early neonatal period [ 28 ].

Despite earlier diagnosis from earlier indications of disease onset, the median lifespan for untreated MPS IH patients is under 10 years [15] , whereas the median lifespan for untreated MPS IA patients is longer, with the majority of patients living into adulthood [15] , [30] .
